title: Ask now, collect later
description:
`std::async` starts a function running (here, on another thread) and immediately hands back a `std::future`: a ticket you can redeem later for the result with `.get()`.

Write `std::vector<int> mapAsync(const std::vector<int>& inputs, int (*work)(int))`.

For each input it launches `work(input)` with `std::async(std::launch::async, ...)`, keeping the futures in a vector. Then it collects every result **in the original order** and returns them.

Launch them all first and only then start calling `.get()`. If you call `.get()` inside the launching loop, each task finishes before the next begins and nothing runs in parallel.
hints: First loop: `futures.push_back(std::async(std::launch::async, work, input));`. Second loop: `results.push_back(f.get());` for each future in order.
lessonTitle: Futures, Promises, std::async and Thread Pools
